newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ottawa landmine ban signing set for Dec 2-4.
newsitem.headline: Ottawa landmine ban signing set for Dec 2-4.

text.p: An international conference in Ottawa at which a treaty banning landmines is to be signed will be held from December 2 to 4, the Canadian embassy in Brussels said on Friday.

In a statement released at the four-day Brussels Conference on a Global Ban on Anti-personnel Mines, Canada invited countries to "sign a legally binding treaty to ban the use, stockpiling, production and transfer of anti-personnel landmines".

"It is now clear we will reach this goal (of banning landmines). From December 2 to 4 we will be able to establish a new global norm against these horrible weapons," ambassador Lloyd Axworthy said in the statement.
At the latest count 95 countries have signed the so-called Brussels Declaration forming the basis for negotiations in Oslo, Norway, in September on the exact wording of the Ottawa treaty.

A total of 115 countries took part in the Brussels talks but 37, including the United States, attended as observers only. The United States will not sign because it favours separate United Nations-sponsored landmine talks in Geneva.
The other observers include Cuba, India, Indonesia, Iran, Israel, Libya, Pakistan, the Palestinian Authority and Turkey.
